en: Magellan turned Venus from a featureless cloud-veiled disc into a mapped planet. Launched from Shuttle Atlantis's payload bay 1989-05-04 — the first planetary spacecraft to ride a Shuttle — and arrived at Venus 1990-08-10 via a long Type-IV trajectory (1.5 solar revolutions). Over four mapping cycles the synthetic-aperture radar imaged 98% of Venus's surface at ~120-m resolution, revealing tessera highlands, coronae, pancake domes, and a young, volcanically-resurfaced surface. Mission ended 1994-10-13 in the Termination Experiment — the first planned controlled atmospheric entry of a planetary spacecraft.

en: The Emirates Mars Mission — Al Amal, 'Hope' — was conceived in 2014 to mark the 50th anniversary of UAE federation in 2021. en: Vostok 5 set a record that still stands. Valery Bykovsky flew nearly five days alone in orbit — eighty-one laps of the planet — which remains, six decades on, the longest solo spaceflight anyone has ever made. It was an endurance test above all, pushing a single cosmonaut and a small spacecraft far past the day Titov managed, to see whether a person could simply keep going. He could. And Bykovsky wasn't even the headline of his own mission: two days into his flight, Vostok 6 went up carrying the first woman in space, and the world's attention went with her.

en: By the last Gemini, one problem was still unsolved: spacewalking didn't work. The flights between Ed White and Gemini 12 had turned EVA into a series of exhausting near-failures — astronauts fighting for every motion, overheating, running out of time. Buzz Aldrin fixed it, and the fix was preparation: he rehearsed the whole thing underwater until it was routine, and the spacecraft was fitted with handholds, footholds, and tethers so he had something to work against. Across more than five hours outside, he did ordinary tasks calmly and came back unspent — proof that EVA could be made reliable. It was the final item on the Gemini checklist, and with it the program closed, having taught NASA everything the Moon would require.

en: Scott Carpenter's 3-orbit flight — repeated Glenn's MA-6 profile to firm up confidence in the Mercury-Atlas vehicle before attempting the longer Schirra/Cooper flights. Carpenter ran extensive zero-g experiments and observation tasks; the heavy experimental load + a stuck yaw thruster caused him to be ~25° off attitude at retro-fire, overshooting the landing target by ~400 km. The 1 h 7 min recovery delay was widely reported and damaged Carpenter's reputation in NASA management; he never flew again. en: The first "J-mission" — extended-stay scientific Apollo with the new Lunar Roving Vehicle. The LRV gave Scott + Irwin a 27.9 km traverse range (vs the 3.5 km of walking-only Apollo 14), opening the dramatic Hadley-Apennine site at the foot of a 4.5-km mountain range and the edge of the sinuous Hadley Rille. Three EVAs totalling 18 h 35 m, 77 kg of samples returned, including the famous "Genesis Rock" (sample 15415) — a 4.1-billion-year-old anorthosite confirming the magma-ocean origin of the lunar highlands crust. Scott's televised "hammer-feather drop" verified Galileo's law of gravitation live. Worden in lunar orbit operated a SIM-bay full of remote-sensing instruments (mapping cameras, gamma-ray, X-ray, alpha-particle spectrometers) and performed the first deep-space EVA on the way home (~39-minute EVA at ~317 000 km from Earth to retrieve the film canisters). Apollo 15's recovery was marred by one of three parachutes failing to deploy — CM splashed down hard but crew was safe.

en: Apollo 13 was meant to be the third crewed lunar landing, targeted at the Fra Mauro highlands. At 55 hours 54 minutes into the flight an oxygen tank in the Service Module ruptured, crippling the Command-Service Module's electrical and life-support systems. With landing scrubbed, the crew — James Lovell, Jack Swigert, and Fred Haise — powered down the CSM, moved into the Lunar Module Aquarius as a lifeboat, and used the LM's descent engine for a Pericynthion+2-hour burn that placed them on a fast free-return trajectory. They swung past the Moon at 254 km altitude on 1970-04-15 and splashed down safely in the South Pacific on 1970-04-17. The mission is studied today as a model of disciplined real-time engineering improvisation.

en: John Glenn's 3-orbit flight — first American to orbit Earth, 10 months after Gagarin and 4 months after Titov. Orbit: 159 × 265 km, inclination 32.5°. en: New Horizons had exactly one chance and took it. There was no orbit and no way to slow down — nine and a half years of travel, the fastest launch in history, all converging on a few hours at Pluto, executed by a machine so far away that each command took hours to arrive. It nailed the flyby on 14 July 2015 and overturned the expectation of a dead world: Pluto turned out to have mountains of water ice, a vast heart-shaped glacier of frozen nitrogen still slowly churning, and a young, active surface no one thought a body that small and cold could keep. Then it flew on to Arrokoth, a billion kilometres past Pluto — the most distant world ever seen up close — and it is still going.

en: Aurora 7 was meant to be a repeat and became a scare. Scott Carpenter flew the same three-orbit profile as Glenn, but distracted by experiments and a balky control system he burned through his attitude fuel and fired his retros a few seconds late and slightly out of line — enough to carry him some 400 kilometres past his landing target. For a long, silent hour no one knew whether he was alive, until a search plane spotted him bobbing in a life raft. It is a plain reminder that in a machine with almost no margin, small errors compound fast — and that recovering from them is a skill of its own.

en: ESA-led mission with a NASA launch and one instrument contribution. Where Parker Solar Probe goes closer than anyone has ever been, Solar Orbiter goes higher — using repeated Venus gravity assists over a decade to climb out of the ecliptic toward ~33° heliographic inclination. en: Skylab 3 took the endurance question and nearly doubled the answer. Where the first crew had stayed 28 days, Alan Bean's crew stayed 59 — pushing the human body further into long-duration weightlessness than anyone had gone, and returning healthier than the pessimists had feared. They logged a huge haul of solar observations from the Apollo Telescope Mount and rode out a scare when thruster leaks on their Apollo ferry briefly raised the prospect of a rescue flight. Skylab 3 is where long stays in space started to look not just survivable but routine — the quiet groundwork for every months-long station tour since.

en: Apollo-Soyuz is where the space race ends — not at a finish line, but with a handshake. In July 1975 an American Apollo and a Soviet Soyuz, the rival spacecraft of the rival superpowers, met and docked in orbit, and Tom Stafford and Alexei Leonov shook hands through the open hatch between them. It took a jointly-built docking adapter, two crews learning each other's language, and a thaw in the Cold War deep enough to let the era's fiercest competitors cooperate in full view of the world. Nothing about it was strictly necessary; that was the point. After eighteen years of racing to be first, the two programs chose, for one flight, simply to meet — and set the template for the international cooperation that would one day build the Space Station.

en: Juno entered Jupiter orbit 2016-07-05 on a highly elliptical 53-day polar trajectory that takes it from inside the radiation belts (perijove ~4200 km above cloud tops) out past Callisto. Solar-powered — its ~50 m² triple-junction arrays deliver 14 kW at Earth but only ~500 W at Jupiter, the first time solar power has been used at that distance. Confirmed Jupiter has a diluted rocky core (not a sharp boundary), measured the polar cyclone arrangement (eight circumpolar storms around each pole), and imaged Io’s volcanism at unprecedented detail in 2023. Extended mission includes flybys of all four Galilean moons through 2025.

en: Gordon Cooper's 22-orbit flight — last Mercury mission and last solo American spaceflight ever (all subsequent US programmes flew multi-person crews). en: Carr, Gibson and Pogue — the final and longest Skylab crew, 84 days 1 hour, all-rookie. Launched 1973-11-16 14:01 UTC on Saturn IB (SA-208). The mission is best remembered for what NASA later called a 'Skylab mutiny' or 'strike' — a disputed account of a rest-day stand-down around day 42 after relentless ground-controller demands compressed every minute of waking time; NASA and the crew have stated no organised strike occurred, but the underlying timeline overload was real and led to permanent NASA reforms on crew time-line planning for long-duration missions. Splashed down 1974-02-08 15:17 UTC — the last Skylab splashdown. CSM-118 displayed at the National Museum of the US Air Force, Dayton OH.

en: ESA's first lunar mission and the first European spacecraft to reach the Moon. SMART = Small Missions for Advanced Research in Technology — and the key technology was a Hall-effect solar-electric ion thruster (PPS-1350-G), at the time the largest such thruster ever flown. Launched 2003-09-27 as a shared payload on an Ariane 5 from Kourou, the 367-kg spacecraft used its 1.2-kW xenon ion drive over 13 months to slowly raise its Earth orbit, eventually captured by lunar gravity on 2004-11-15 — a 13-month low-thrust spiral rather than the days-long chemical transfer of every prior lunar mission. Operated for 16 months in a polar lunar orbit returning AMIE camera imagery, the first X-ray fluorescence elemental maps of the Moon (D-CIXS), and infrared mineral spectroscopy (SIR). Deliberately impacted Lacus Excellentiae (34.4° S, 46.2° W) on 2006-09-03 05:42 UTC — the impact flash was observed live from the Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope.

en: SpaceIL's Beresheet (Hebrew: 'In the beginning') launched as a shared-ride passenger on a Falcon 9 in February 2019. Instead of a direct trans-lunar injection, the small lander performed weeks of perigee-raising phasing burns to climb from a parking orbit out to the Moon — a fuel-saving trajectory pioneered for low-budget missions. SpaceIL committed to a successor (Beresheet 2) within days.

en: The first crewed Apollo flight, 21 months after the Apollo 1 fire (1967-01-27) killed Grissom, White and Chaffee on the pad. Apollo 7 verified the redesigned Block II Command and Service Module in Earth orbit — life support, power, propulsion (SPS fired eight times), thermal control, and the world's first live TV broadcast from a crewed US spacecraft. Schirra (head cold + irritable throughout) overruled Houston on a re-entry helmet question, contributing to Mission Control's decision that none of the three crewmembers would fly again. The 10 day 20 hour flight cleared the way for Apollo 8's lunar-orbit gamble two months later.

en: OSIRIS-REx carried out one of the most exacting asteroid-proximity operations ever attempted. Launched 2016-09-08 from Cape Canaveral on an Atlas V 411, used a 2017 Earth gravity assist to rotate its orbital plane onto Bennu's 6° inclination, and rendezvoused with the 492-m carbonaceous near-Earth asteroid 2018-12-03. After stationkeeping at ~19 km, it later entered a record ~1.4 km orbit — the closest spacecraft orbit ever around any celestial body. Spent two years mapping Bennu's boulder-strewn surface and discovering active particle ejections. 2020-10-20 the Touch-and-Go sample arm descended to the Nightingale site, fired N₂ gas into the surface, and grabbed a plume — sinking 50 cm into a 'rubble-pile fluid' surface. Sample Return Capsule delivered 121.6 g of Bennu material to Utah 2023-09-24. The spacecraft itself was immediately redesignated OSIRIS-APEX, en route to a 2029 Apophis rendezvous.

en: Yuri Gagarin's 108-minute single-orbit flight — the first crewed spaceflight in history, and the first human to orbit Earth. Launched 1961-04-12 06:07 UTC from Baikonur on a Vostok-K (8K72K) launcher; orbit 169 × 327 km, inclination 65°. The spherical descent module ejected Gagarin at ~7 km altitude (a fact the USSR concealed for years to claim full crewed landing under FAI rules). Gagarin parachuted to Smelovka, Saratov Oblast; the capsule landed separately and is on display at the RKK Energia Museum in Korolyov, Russia. The flight ended Korolev's decade-long missile / satellite work and triggered the U.S. crewed-spaceflight programme + Kennedy's Moon-landing pledge six weeks later.

en: Korolev's polished aluminium sphere — 58 cm wide, 83.6 kg, two transmitters on 20.005 and 40.002 MHz — became the first human-made object to reach orbit on 1957-10-04 19:28 UTC. The 215 × 939 km, 65.1° trajectory beeped over America that night and again every 96 minutes, audible on shortwave to anyone who tuned in. Batteries depleted on 1957-10-26 (after 21 days, ~315 orbits); the satellite decayed and burned up on re-entry 1958-01-04 after roughly 1440 orbits. The flight was an OKB-1 side project: Korolev needed a lightweight payload for his still-developmental R-7 ICBM and pitched 'PS-1' (Prosteyshiy Sputnik — 'simplest satellite') to Khrushchev as a propaganda coup. It worked. The shock in Washington triggered ARPA (founded 1958-02), the National Aeronautics and Space Act (signed 1958-07), and Kennedy's Moon-landing pledge four years later. Sputnik 1 also returned the first orbital ionospheric and atmospheric-density data — engineers used the Doppler shift on the 20 / 40 MHz carriers to map air density at 215 km, work that fed into every subsequent re-entry calculation.

India became the fourth space agency at Mars and the first to succeed on its first try.

en: Hera is the European Space Agency's contribution to humanity's first planetary-defence experiment. In 2022 NASA's DART spacecraft deliberately crashed into Dimorphos — the small moon of the asteroid Didymos — and measurably shortened its orbit. Hera, launched in October 2024 on a Falcon 9, is flying to the same binary asteroid (with a 2025 Mars gravity assist en route) to conduct the detailed post-impact survey DART couldn't: the size of the crater, Dimorphos's mass and internal structure, and precisely how much momentum the impact transferred. Together, DART and Hera turn a one-off demonstration into a repeatable, well-characterised deflection technique. Hera carries two CubeSats, Juventas and Milani, for close-up radar sounding and mineralogy.
old: Hera هي مساهمة وكالة الفضاء الأوروبية في أول تجربة للدفاع الكوكبي للبشرية. في عام 2022 اصطدمت مركبة DART الفضائية التابعة لـ NASA عمداً بديمورفوس — القمر الصغير للكويكب ديديموس — وقصّرت مداره بشكل قابل للقياس. انطلقت Hera في أكتوبر 2024 على صاروخ Falcon 9، وهي تتجه إلى نفس الكويكب الثنائي (مع مساعدة جاذبية المريخ في عام 2025 في الطريق) لإجراء المسح التفصيلي لما بعد الاصطدام الذي لم تستطع DART القيام به: حجم الحفرة، وكتلة ديمورفوس وبنيته الداخلية، وبالضبط كمية الزخم التي نقلها الاصطدام. معاً، تحوّل DART وHera عرضاً توضيحياً لمرة واحدة إلى تقنية انحراف قابلة للتكرار ومحددة بشكل جيد. تحمل Hera قمرين صناعيين صغيرين من نوع CubeSats هما Juventas وMilani، للسبر الراداري عن قرب ودراسة علم المعادن.

en: Blue Origin's first cargo Blue Moon lander, contracted under NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) program. A single-stage descent vehicle powered by the BE-7 cryogenic engine, designed to deliver up to ~3 tonnes of payload to the lunar surface. Launches on Blue Origin's New Glenn from Cape Canaveral, performs trans-lunar injection on the New Glenn second stage, then executes lunar orbit insertion and powered descent. The Mark 1 cargo flight precedes the human-rated Mark 2, which NASA contracted for crewed Artemis landings — now one of the two candidate landers for Artemis IV and later missions.

en: By Apollo 15 the race was long over, and the science took the wheel — literally. This was the first flight to carry the Lunar Rover, which turned a two-mile walking radius into a proper eighteen-mile field expedition, and it set down not on a safe flat plain but in a valley between a mountain range and a winding canyon. Scott and Irwin came home with the "Genesis Rock," a four-billion-year-old shard of the Moon's original crust that confirmed how it had formed. Apollo had stopped visiting the Moon and started studying it — and it kept getting better at that right up until it was cancelled.

en: NASA Discovery-program mission, led by Johns Hopkins University APL. Launched 1996-02-17, NEAR Shoemaker flew past asteroid 253 Mathilde (1997-06-27) before an Earth gravity assist (1998-01-23) phased its orbit to match Eros. Orbital insertion around 433 Eros on 2000-02-14 began a 12-month survey that returned 160,000 images and complete spectral, compositional, and gravitational maps of the 34 × 11 × 11 km S-type body. On 2001-02-12, five orbit-lowering burns brought the spacecraft to 5 km altitude; controlled descent at ~1.7 m/s ended with a soft landing near the Himeros saddle (35°N, 280°W), returning images to within 125 m of the surface. The spacecraft survived and transmitted from the surface for ~16 days.

en: Jared Isaacman, Sian Proctor, Hayley Arceneaux and Chris Sembroski — the first orbital flight crewed entirely by people who were not professional government astronauts. Launched 2021-09-15 00:02 UTC from LC-39A on Falcon 9 B1062 (third flight), atop Crew Dragon Resilience (C207, previously flown on Crew-1). Reached a 585 km circular orbit at 51.6° inclination — the highest crewed orbit since the Hubble servicing missions. No docking with any station; three days of free flight including the first onboard cupola (replacing the docking adapter). Splashed down off the Florida coast 2021-09-18 23:06 UTC. The mission raised over $243M for St. Jude Children's Research Hospital — Arceneaux is a former St. Jude patient and the first cancer survivor in orbit.

en: Soviet–ESA flagship of the Halley armada. Vega 1 launched 1984-12-15 with a Venera-lineage lander plus a first-of-kind ESA/CNES-built helium balloon that drifted in Venus's cloud deck at 54 km altitude for 46.5 hours, transmitting wind + temperature data via a 20-station global radio net. After dropping its descent module the bus used Venus gravity assist to redirect to comet 1P/Halley, achieving a 8890 km closest approach on 1986-03-06 — the first cometary nucleus encounter, and the position fix that ESA's Giotto used to navigate its own much closer Halley flyby a week later.

en: Opportunity (MER-B) hit a planetary jackpot — its airbag-cocooned lander bounced 26 times across Meridiani Planum and rolled into a 22-m crater (Eagle) by sheer luck, surrounded by exposed bedrock a rover could read without driving. First images showed jarosite + "blueberry" hematite concretions, the strongest mineral evidence to that point of standing liquid water on early Mars. Over 14 years 138 days (5,111 sols) Opportunity traversed 45.16 km — the Mars rover marathon record — visiting Endurance, Victoria, and Endeavour craters. A planet-wide dust storm in June 2018 blocked sunlight from its solar panels; final transmission was 2018-06-10, and NASA declared end-of-mission 2019-02-13.

en: The first crewed mission to leave low Earth orbit, the first to escape Earth gravity, and the first to orbit the Moon. Launched 1968-12-21 on the first crewed flight of the Saturn V (AS-503), Apollo 8 entered lunar orbit on Christmas Eve 1968. Anders' "Earthrise" photograph during the fourth orbit became one of the most influential images in history. The crew read from Genesis on live television to ~1 billion viewers — the largest TV audience to that date. 10 orbits later they fired the SPS engine for TEI on the far side of the Moon, returning to Pacific splashdown 1968-12-27. NASA had decided in August 1968 to swap Apollo 8's payload from a high-Earth-orbit LM test to a lunar-orbit CSM-only mission after CIA intelligence suggested the USSR might attempt a circumlunar flight first.

en: Joint NASA-ESA-ASI mission. After a 7-year cruise using gravity assists at Venus, Earth, and Jupiter, Cassini entered Saturn orbit 2004-07-01 and operated for 13 years, completing 294 orbits and 162 close moon flybys. It discovered Enceladus’s south-polar plumes (active water-ice geysers), mapped Titan’s methane lakes via radar, and resolved Saturn’s hexagonal polar storm. The Grand Finale (April–September 2017) wove 22 orbits through the gap between the rings and the cloud tops, ending with a controlled atmospheric entry to prevent any chance of contaminating Enceladus or Titan with terrestrial microbes.

en: Launched 1966-03-31 from Baikonur, Luna 10 became the first spacecraft to orbit the Moon — and the first artificial satellite of any body other than Earth — when it inserted into a 350 × 1017 km lunar orbit at 71.9° inclination on 1966-04-03. Two and a half years before Apollo 8 reached the Moon with humans aboard. Carried a magnetometer, gamma-ray spectrometer, infrared radiometer, micrometeoroid detectors, plasma sensors, and a radio probe of the lunar gravity field. The gamma-ray data was the first compositional remote sensing of the Moon, suggesting basalt-like mare composition. Famously broadcast the Internationale anthem during the 23rd Congress of the Soviet Communist Party on 1966-04-04 — a propaganda flourish more than science. Operated 56 days / 460 orbits before its NiCd batteries depleted on 1966-05-30; remains in lunar orbit.

en: Voskhod 1 was the first flight to carry more than one person into space, and it managed it by subtraction. There was no room in the one-seat Vostok for a three-person crew, so the engineers took things out — the ejection seats that had saved every previous cosmonaut, and, because even then it was too tight, the pressure suits. Komarov, Feoktistov, and Yegorov flew for a day in shirtsleeves, with no way to escape a launch or reentry emergency and no protection if the cabin lost air. Nothing went wrong, so it looked like a triumph. It was really a bet — that the corners cut to score a first wouldn't be the ones that mattered — and it happened to win.
old: كانت Voskhod 1 أول رحلة تحمل أكثر من شخص واحد إلى الفضاء، وقد حققت ذلك بالحذف. لم يكن هناك مكان في Vostok ذات المقعد الواحد لطاقم مكون من ثلاثة أشخاص، لذا أزال المهندسون أشياء — مقاعد القذف التي أنقذت كل رائد فضاء سابق، ولأن المساحة ظلت ضيقة حتى بعد ذلك، أزالوا بدلات الضغط. طار كوماروف وفيوكتيستوف ويغوروف لمدة يوم بأكمام القمصان، دون أي وسيلة للهروب من طوارئ الإطلاق أو العودة ودون حماية في حال فقدت المقصورة الهواء. لم يحدث خطأ، لذا بدا الأمر وكأنه انتصار. كان في الواقع رهانًا — أن الزوايا التي تم قطعها لتحقيق السبق لن تكون تلك التي تهم — وقد كُتب له الفوز.

en: Pavel Belyayev + Alexei Leonov's 1-day flight — first EVA in history. Leonov spent 12 min outside Voskhod 2 (1965-03-18 11:34 UTC), pressurised through an inflatable Volga airlock that Soviet engineers added because the Voskhod hull lacked the room for full depressurisation. Leonov's suit ballooned in vacuum, jamming him outside the airlock; he had to vent suit pressure to re-enter, raising decompression-sickness risk. Re-entry was equally dramatic — the automatic landing system failed, and Belyayev manually piloted the descent module to a hard landing in deep Urals snow ~390 km off-target; the crew survived two nights in the forest among wolves before rescue helicopters arrived 1965-03-21. The cabin atmosphere also became O₂-rich in orbit, after the EVA hatch failed to re-seal, briefly risking spontaneous combustion.

en: The full dress rehearsal for the first lunar landing. Stafford and Cernan flew LM Snoopy down to ~15.6 km altitude above the planned Apollo 11 landing site at Mare Tranquillitatis — every step of a landing approach except the actual landing itself. They confirmed the descent profile, the landing radar, the ascent trajectory, and the rendezvous procedure that Apollo 11 would use two months later. The LM's ascent-stage propellant tanks were deliberately underfueled (~50 % of nominal) to prevent any temptation to attempt a landing. Snoopy's ascent stage was the only one to leave lunar orbit with positive ∆v — jettisoned into a heliocentric orbit where it remains today, intermittently re-detected by amateur astronomers (most recently confirmed by Nick Howes / Faulkes Telescope, 2019).

en: First spacecraft to visit Mercury, first to fly past two planets, and first to use a gravity assist to reach its destination. Launched 1973-11-03 05:45 UTC from Cape Canaveral LC-36B on Atlas SLV-3D Centaur AC-34. Mariner 10 swung past Venus on 1974-02-05 (5768 km closest approach, first UV cloud-belt imaging of Venus) using the encounter to drop its perihelion into Mercury's orbital realm — the first deliberate gravity-assist trajectory in space history. Made three Mercury flybys: 1974-03-29 (703 km), 1974-09-21 (48069 km), and 1975-03-16 (327 km). Imaged ~45% of Mercury's surface — the only resolved imagery available until MESSENGER (2008-2015). Discovered Mercury's intrinsic magnetic field and thin sodium-helium exosphere. Solar-array temperature management was an open mission engineering problem: project scientists tilted the panels and rolled the spacecraft to keep them under 115°C. Mission ended 1975-03-24 when attitude-control nitrogen propellant was depleted; spacecraft is presumed to be in heliocentric orbit, periodically passing Mercury.

en: The lunar far side has no direct radio line of sight to Earth. To land a spacecraft there, China first launched the Queqiao relay satellite to a halo orbit around Earth-Moon Lagrange point L2 — a vantage point that sees both the far side and Earth simultaneously. With that infrastructure in place, Chang'e 4 became the first spacecraft to soft-land on the far side. The Yutu-2 rover has been operating since January 2019 and has driven ~1.6 km as of 2024, making it the longest-operating lunar rover in history.

en: Joint ESA / JAXA mission to Mercury, launched 2018-10-20 — named after Italian mathematician Giuseppe (Bepi) Colombo, who designed Mariner 10's multi-flyby trajectory. The 8-year cruise uses 9 gravity assists (Earth 2020, Venus 2020, Venus 2021, then six Mercury flybys 2021–2025) plus continuous ion-electric thrust from the Mercury Transfer Module to bleed off the enormous solar-gravity gradient between Earth and Mercury orbits. Mercury orbit insertion 2026-11-21; science operations begin early 2027 after MTM jettison and separation of the two orbiters — ESA's MPO (planetary surface + composition) and JAXA's Mio (magnetosphere). Tests of general relativity via radio-science range tracking through Mercury's strong solar-gravity environment are also planned.

en: Artemis III no longer lands on the Moon. In February 2026 NASA changed the plan: before risking a landing, a crew will fly Orion in low Earth orbit and rehearse the hardest new step — rendezvous and docking with the commercial landers that will later carry astronauts to the surface. SLS launches Orion with four crew, flying with a spacer in place of its upper stage, since no push towards the Moon is needed. In orbit, Orion meets pathfinder versions of SpaceX's Starship lander and Blue Origin's Blue Moon, docks, and the crew test the joined vehicles' life support, communications and propulsion, along with the new AxEMU spacesuits. The flight lasts about two weeks. It plays the part Apollo 9 played in 1969, when the lunar module was flown and docked in Earth orbit before anyone took it to the Moon. Crew, named in June 2026: Randy Bresnik (commander), Luca Parmitano of ESA (pilot), Andre Douglas and Frank Rubio. NASA plans the flight for 2027.

en: Gemini 8 made the first docking of two spacecraft in orbit — and then nearly killed its crew. Minutes after Neil Armstrong eased his Gemini into a locked joint with an Agena target, the linked pair began to roll, faster and faster, until it was tumbling roughly once a second and the astronauts' vision was starting to gray toward blackout. Armstrong undocked — which only made it worse, since the fault was in his own spacecraft — then shut down the main thrusters and stopped the spin with the reentry-control system, a decision that saved their lives but, by the rules, forced an immediate emergency return. It was the program's most dangerous moment, and it was Armstrong's first spaceflight. The calm, fast diagnosis under a failing situation is exactly the temperament NASA would remember when it chose who would land on the Moon.
old: حققت Gemini 8 أول التحام لمركبتين فضائيتين في المدار — ثم كادت تودي بحياة طاقمها. فبعد دقائق من إدخال نيل آرمسترونغ مركبته Gemini برفق في وصلة مقفلة مع الهدف Agena، بدأ الزوج المتصل يدور، أسرع فأسرع، حتى صار يدور نحو مرة كل ثانية وبدأت رؤية رواد الفضاء تعتم قرب الإغماء. فصل آرمسترونغ الالتحام — وهو ما زاد الأمر سوءاً، لأن العطل كان في مركبته هو — ثم أوقف الدافعات الرئيسية وأوقف الدوران بنظام التحكم في العودة، وهو قرار أنقذ حياتهما لكنه فرض، بحسب القواعد، عودة طارئة فورية. كانت أخطر لحظة في البرنامج، وكانت أول رحلة فضائية لآرمسترونغ. والتشخيص الهادئ السريع في موقف يتدهور هو بالضبط الطباع التي ستتذكرها NASA حين تختار من سيهبط على القمر.

en: Pioneer 10 was the trail-blazer — first to cross the asteroid belt (which we then learned was much less hazardous than predicted), first to image Jupiter at close range, first to reach a heliocentric distance greater than Pluto’s perihelion (1983). It carries the Pioneer plaque designed by Carl Sagan, Frank Drake, and Linda Salzman Sagan — humanity’s first deliberate interstellar message. Final successful contact 2003-01-23 from ~82 AU; the spacecraft now drifts toward the constellation Taurus, with an encounter near Aldebaran in roughly two million years.

en: The first crewed flight of the Lunar Module. In Earth orbit, McDivitt and Schweickart undocked LM Spider from CSM Gumdrop, flew up to 183 km away over six hours, then rendezvous and re-docked — every step of the lunar-rendezvous procedure tested without the option of bringing the crew home in the CSM if anything went wrong. Schweickart did a 38-minute EVA on the LM porch, demonstrating the Apollo EVA spacesuit + PLSS backpack design that the Moonwalking crews would use. Scott did a stand-up EVA from the CSM hatch. With LM hardware and rendezvous procedures verified, NASA was clear to send Apollo 10 to the Moon two months later.

en: Faith 7 closed Mercury, and did it the hard way. Gordon Cooper flew twenty-two orbits over a day and a half — longer than every previous Mercury flight combined — and then, in the final hours, his automatic control system failed. So he flew the reentry by hand, lining the capsule up against the horizon and the stars and firing his retros on a spoken count, and put it down closer to the ship than any flight before. It was the last time an American flew in space alone, and a fitting last word for a program built by test pilots: when the automation quit, the pilot brought it home.

en: Perseverance is the most ambitious Mars surface mission ever flown. Mars Sample Return depends on it — the rover is collecting and caching samples in tubes that a future mission will retrieve and bring to Earth. Ingenuity, the first helicopter on another planet, flew 72 missions before retiring with damaged rotors in January 2024 — proving controlled flight is possible in Mars's thin atmosphere. MOXIE, an oxygen-from-CO2 demonstrator, produced the first locally-made oxygen on another planet, a rehearsal for crewed Mars missions.
old: Perseverance هي الأكثر طموحاً من بين جميع مهام سطح المريخ التي تم إطلاقها حتى الآن. مهمة جلب عينات المريخ تعتمد عليها — فالمسبار يجمع العينات وتخزينها في أنابيب ستسترجعها مهمة مستقبلية وتحضرها إلى الأرض. Ingenuity، أول مروحية على كوكب آخر، نفذت 72 مهمة قبل أن تتوقف عن العمل بسبب تضرر أجنحتها في يناير 2024 — مما أثبت أن الطيران المحكوم ممكن في الغلاف الجوي الرقيق للمريخ. MOXIE، جهاز توليد الأكسجين من CO2، أنتجت أول أكسجين محلي الصنع على كوكب آخر، وهي بمثابة بروفة استعداداً لمهام المريخ التي سيقودها الإنسان.
new: Perseverance هي أكثر مهام سطح المريخ طموحاً من بين كل ما أُرسل حتى الآن. وتعتمد عليها مهمة إعادة عينات المريخ — إذ تجمع المركبة الجوالة العينات وتخزنها في أنابيب ستستردها مهمة مستقبلية وتحملها إلى الأرض. وقد نفّذت Ingenuity، أول مروحية على كوكب آخر، 72 رحلة طيران قبل أن تتقاعد بسبب تضرر شفراتها الدوارة في يناير 2024، مثبتةً إمكانية الطيران المتحكَّم به في الغلاف الجوي الرقيق للمريخ. وأنتج MOXIE، وهو جهاز تجريبي لتوليد الأكسجين من CO2، أول أكسجين يُصنَّع محلياً على كوكب آخر، في بروفة لمهام المريخ المأهولة.

en: Designed primarily as a Strategic Defense Initiative technology demonstrator, Clementine spent 10 weeks in lunar orbit returning the first systematic global topographic and multispectral map of the Moon. Bistatic radar measurements at the lunar south pole produced the first tantalising hints of water ice — confirmed years later by Lunar Prospector and Chandrayaan-1. The follow-on mission to flyby the asteroid Geographos failed when a thruster malfunction depleted the spacecraft's propellant.

en: JAXA's follow-on to the original Hayabusa. Launched 2014-12-03, Hayabusa2 reached carbonaceous near-Earth asteroid (162173) Ryugu on 2018-06-27 after a 3.5-year low-thrust ion cruise + Earth gravity assist. Surface operations 2018–2019: two touchdown-and-go sample collections bracketing a Small Carry-on Impactor experiment (2019-04-05) that excavated a 14 m crater for the second sample. Three MINERVA-II rovers returned the first surface images from an asteroid; the DLR/CNES MASCOT lander operated for 17 hours. Sample return capsule reentry over Woomera on 2020-12-05 (UTC; recovered 2020-12-06 local/JST) delivered 5.4 g of pristine Ryugu material — the first asteroid sample with subsurface stratigraphy. Extended mission: flyby of 98943 Torifune (2001 CC21) in 2026-07; rendezvous with fast-rotating (1998 KY26) targeted for 2031-07.

en: Until SLIM, lunar landings had a kilometre-scale targeting accuracy. JAXA's Smart Lander demonstrated 100 m accuracy — the precision required for crewed missions to dock with pre-positioned cargo, for sample-return ascent vehicles to find their orbital partners, and for any future architecture that depends on landing at specific scientifically valuable sites. SLIM also pioneered low-energy ballistic transfer to the Moon, taking 135 days to arrive but using less propellant than direct trajectories. A demonstration of the patience interplanetary missions can afford when timeline isn't the binding constraint.

en: The first crewed flight of the Soyuz spacecraft, launched 23 April 1967 with Vladimir Komarov aboard. The rushed vehicle suffered cascading failures in orbit — an undeployed solar panel, attitude-control problems — and the mission was cut short. en: Perseverance went to Mars to look for the dead. Landed in 2021 on the floor of Jezero Crater — a basin holding the delta of a river that fed a lake billions of years ago, exactly the kind of place life would have left traces — it is the first rover built specifically to search for signs of ancient life, and to do something no mission had done: seal Martian rock into tubes and set them aside for a future spacecraft to carry home. It also delivered Ingenuity, the small helicopter that made the first powered flight on another planet. If the samples it is caching are ever returned, they will be the first pieces of another planet’s surface brought back to Earth.

en: Akatsuki — "dawn" — was Japan's first Venus mission. Launched 2010-05-20 from Tanegashima on an H-IIA 202, paired with the IKAROS solar-sail demonstrator. The planned Venus orbit insertion 2010-12-07 failed when salt crystal buildup in an oxidiser check valve threw the main engine off-axis 152 seconds into the burn. JAXA kept the spacecraft alive in solar orbit for five years, twelve correction maneuvers, until the next Venus encounter window. On 2015-12-07 a 1228-second burn using four attitude-control thrusters — never designed for orbital insertion — placed Akatsuki into a highly elliptical 400 × 440,000 km, 3°-inclination orbit. One of the most dramatic mission-saves in spaceflight history. Contact was lost in 2024; JAXA declared operations complete on 2025-09-18.

en: Friendship 7 is the flight where the United States finally caught its breath. John Glenn was the first American to orbit — three times around the planet, ten months after Gagarin — and for a country that had spent four years watching the Soviets go first, that was enough to make him the most famous man in the nation overnight. The drama came near the end: a faulty sensor suggested his heat shield might be loose, and controllers had him keep his spent retro-pack strapped on through reentry as a long shot to hold it in place. It held. Glenn came home, and the anxiety that had hung over the whole program lifted with him.

en: First three-crew spaceflight in history. Komarov, Feoktistov and Yegorov flew 1964-10-12 to 1964-10-13 in a heavily modified Vostok capsule (designated Voskhod / 'Sunrise'). Ejection seats were removed and the cabin pressure system re-rated to allow three men to sit in shirtsleeves — a propaganda victory against the planned US Gemini two-crew flights, but a brutal compromise that left the crew with no escape capability during launch or re-entry. Cabin spacing was so tight Komarov reported he could feel Yegorov's breath on his neck for 24 hours. Landed 1964-10-13 07:47 UTC near Marevka, Kazakhstan, using the new soft-landing solid-rocket retro system because no parachute ejection was possible. While they were in orbit, Khrushchev was deposed; the crew returned to a fully different Soviet leadership.

en: Soyuz 1 is the flight that killed a cosmonaut, and it should never have flown. The new Soyuz spacecraft was rushed into service under political pressure with hundreds of known unresolved faults — engineers reportedly pleaded to delay — and in orbit it began to fail: a solar panel wouldn't deploy, the attitude control fought the pilot. Vladimir Komarov flew it down anyway, and on reentry the parachutes tangled and failed. He hit the ground at full speed. It was the first death in the history of human spaceflight, and its cause was less bad luck than a program that couldn't afford to admit its machine wasn't ready — the exact failure the culture of hidden, must-succeed firsts had been building toward.

en: ESA's flagship comet-rendezvous mission. After a 10-year cruise that wove three Earth assists, a Mars assist, two asteroid flybys, and 957 days of deep-space hibernation, Rosetta caught up with comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko in August 2014 and orbited it for over two years through perihelion and out the back side. The Philae lander reached 67P's surface 2014-11-12 — the first soft landing on a comet — and returned ~64 hours of science after a harpoon failure left it in the shadow of a cliff. Rosetta itself ended the mission with a controlled descent to 67P's surface on 2016-09-30. Key results: organic molecules and glycine in the coma; 67P's initially-measured D/H ratio (≈3× terrestrial) argued against Jupiter-family comets as Earth's water source — a result a 2024 re-analysis has since called into question after finding a measurement error; the first detailed maps of comet outgassing geometry.

en: Soyuz 11 achieved something extraordinary and then lost its crew in the last minutes of the flight. Georgy Dobrovolsky, Vladislav Volkov, and Viktor Patsayev became the first people to live aboard a space station, spending twenty-two days aboard Salyut 1 — and then, during reentry, a valve jolted open at the instant the modules separated and let their cabin air hiss out into space. They wore no pressure suits; there had been no room for suits when the couches were fitted for three. Within seconds, at the edge of space, all three were dead. The capsule landed itself, perfectly on target; the recovery team opened it to find the crew still strapped in their seats. They remain the only human beings to have died in space — and the price bought a rule that has held ever since: crews wear pressure suits through launch and reentry, always.

en: Voskhod 2 achieved the first spacewalk and nearly turned it into the first death in space. Alexei Leonov floated out of an inflatable airlock into vacuum, the first human ever fully outside a spacecraft — and then his suit ballooned so stiff he couldn't bend to get back in. He had to open a valve and bleed his own air out, courting the bends, just to shrink enough to fit through the hatch. It wasn't over: the automatic reentry failed, the crew flew down by hand, and they landed hundreds of kilometres off course in the frozen Siberian forest, where they waited out two nights among wolves before rescuers reached them on skis. The public saw twelve triumphant minutes; how close it came stayed secret for years.
